---
title: Pure semantic record construction and historical custody projection
date-created: 2026-09-27
type: fabrication specification
status: closed behavioral order; input packet and private receiving commitment required before generation
derived-from: 2026-09-27-muse-assist-journal-operation-lld.md
derived-from-sha256: 2801147e2a97ec18d4e6a7db5e5a73819ad247dd4215d3b5c405c251fd229ce8
---

## Receiving effect and scope

Realize the pure portion of L-O08–L-O13: construct content-identified record witnesses, preserve historical row occurrences as artifacts with separately attributed migration witnesses, and recover original content/time without erasing contrary or unavailable evidence. This is a dependency of the connected storage/application replacement, not a standalone assistant or migration completion. Create exactly Code `src/semiotic-eavt/semantic-record.mjs`. No host writer, query entrypoint or package export is replaced by this order; their connected retirement remains required by L-O06/L-O10. The new module is unmounted until the Systems integration supplies admitted journal capabilities. Do not introduce filesystem, process, clock, provider, storage or authority effects.

Use the existing bounded JSON, SEN, content identity, artifact and journal witness primitives. Allowed imports are JSON canonicalizeJson/admitCanonicalJson/canonicalJson/JSON_RESOURCE_ENVELOPE from the existing JSON package; EMPTY_WITNESS_ROOT/identifyJsonSemanticContent from the relative SEN runtime; jsonToTerm/termToJson from its JSON codec; tm from its notation; seavtRow/normalizeSeavtRow from the existing local row modules; journalWitness/parseJournalWitness from `./journal/event.mjs`; addressArtifact/verifyArtifact/isArtifactRef from `./identity/index.mjs`; and eavtKey/toEavt from the EAVT row package. Import only needed names. Do not import `journal/filesystem/events.mjs`, either old record/query host, or System code. TextEncoder and Date are available pure standard primitives. No bespoke JSON parser, content hash, SEN codec or witness identity implementation.

## F-R01 — Common value and refusal boundary

Export exactly the four functions below. Arguments containing JSON are admitted through canonicalizeJson with JSON_RESOURCE_ENVELOPE before field access; this rejects accessors, custom prototypes, sparse arrays, unpaired surrogates and non-JSON material without invoking a toJSON convenience. The resolver argument is a separate trusted in-process function. Hostile proxies are outside the parsed-JSON transport contract. Verify the imported envelope matches the existing v1 values (source/canonical bytes 1048576, depth 64, nodes 100000, object members 4096, array length 65536, string bytes 262144, key bytes 1024); refuse incompatible change.

All input/result objects below are closed; optional fields are explicitly named. Admit all constructed JSON results within that same aggregate envelope, including witnesses/artifact bodies, and return deeply frozen copies independent of mutable inputs. Never mutate an input. Each function returns synchronously; it has no asynchronous effects. Known input/JSON/SEN/artifact/witness validation failures throw TypeError with code `semantic-record-invalid` and a bounded message naming a field/constraint without embedding content or source paths. Missing required artifact resolution throws TypeError with code `semantic-record-evidence-unavailable`. Propagate exceptions thrown by the trusted resolver unchanged, preserving the owner's JournalUnavailable identity; do not flatten storage failure into invalid input or empty success. No helper output includes admitted, durable, appended, created or an authorization verdict.

Identifiers objectKind/category/origin/operator are nonempty strings of at most 512 Unicode scalar values. Reference arrays are arrays of syntactically valid artifact references in strictly increasing ordinal order; do not silently repair duplicates/order. A JSON snapshot is obtained before comparison, construction or hashing.

## F-R02 — Modern candidate construction

`semanticRecordCandidates(input)` takes required objectKind, category, record, recordedAt, told; optional relation, causes, origin. told is exactly `{for:boolean,against:boolean}` with no positive default. relation, when present, is exactly `{subject,predicate,object}` with JSON values. causes defaults to [] and origin defaults to objectKind only for preservation of the historical wire convention; neither proves authority. Systems supplies authenticated origin where authority matters.

Compute id with identifyJsonSemanticContent({objectKind,value:record,witnessRoot:EMPTY_WITNESS_ROOT}). Construct the record row `{e:jsonToTerm(id),a:jsonToTerm(category),v:jsonToTerm(record),t:recordedAt}` and admit it with seavtRow. Optional relation is a separate row with its subject/predicate/object converted to SEN, and the same original t. Construct witnesses directly with journalWitness using the existing eventForRow law: payload=toEavt(row), address=tm.mark(eavtKey(payload)), time=String(recordedAt), seat=origin, causes=admitted causes, kind=metroplat.journal.observation. Omit referencedArtifacts as the old record constructor does. The claim is tm.mark(`semantic-record.${charge}`), with charge unknown/held/denied/contested from the two independent told booleans; the relation claim is tm.mark("semantic-record.relation"). Preserve existing witness identities for all admitted corresponding inputs; String(t) is only the historical witness boundary representation, never a replacement of row t.

Return exactly `{id,objectKind,told,witnesses}`, record witness first and optional relation second. Empty resulting witness time refuses under the existing witness law. The host separately chooses the feed, publishes, proves admission, barriers and computes its acknowledgment. A pure candidate is never an acknowledgment.

## F-R03 — Historical row artifact

`legacySemanticRowArtifact(value)` takes exactly the L-O11 artifact value and returns exactly `{ref,canonicalText}` from addressArtifact. Enforce its closed fields, literals, safe integer source byte/line/offset/length values and relative path/digest laws. raw must contain no LF, must be nonblank under L-O11's JSON whitespace rule, and UTF-8 byteLength(raw) must equal length. Require offset+length a safe integer no greater than source.bytes. Do not pretend these local checks prove the entire source-file digest or that the bytes were actually observed; the maintenance host checks the source and census.

Parse raw through admitCanonicalJson(raw, JSON_RESOURCE_ENVELOPE), which rejects duplicate keys and malformed text. Pass its value to normalizeSeavtRow and require canonical equality with the supplied row. Preserve the exact raw string, tuple/object form, CR and original t while canonically serializing the artifact. Source.path, line and offset are identity-bearing custody distinctions. No objectKind/category inference, time coercion, support claim or authorship is added. Full-file IO, strict byte decoding before this string boundary, line extraction and blank-line census belong to maintenance, not this pure function.

## F-R04 — Historical migration witness

`legacySemanticImport(rowArtifact, options)` takes a closed `{ref,canonicalText}` and closed options `{operator,importedAt,causes}`. Verify the artifact's exact canonical text and reference, then validate its value through F-R03 and require the same exact pair. importedAt must round-trip as an actual 24-character UTC millisecond timestamp, rejecting normalized invalid dates/offset variants/extended years. causes and operator obey F-R01.

Construct exactly the L-O12 journalWitness observation, with payload pointing to the row artifact, claim semantic-record.legacy-import, address tm.mark(rowArtifact.ref), seat operator, time importedAt, causes and referencedArtifacts [rowArtifact.ref]. Return exactly `{witness,artifacts:[rowArtifact]}`. This does not prove maintenance authority, original authorship, original causes, truth of old content or durable custody. Feed selection/resumption inputs and admission remain Systems responsibilities.

## F-R05 — Pure projection over one admitted source view

`projectSemanticRecords(input, resolveArtifact)` takes closed input `{objectKind,category,witnesses}`; witnesses is an array of supplied journal witnesses. Systems must establish their admitted status and permitted selection before calling. The resolver is a required synchronous function from artifact reference to exact `{ref,canonicalText}` or null/undefined when absent, over the same active verified view. No caller-supplied admission flag or source root is accepted. A Promise/thenable or mismatched resolver result refuses; null/undefined for a required row body gives the evidence-unavailable code. Propagate resolver-thrown exceptions unchanged.

For each supplied witness, use parseJournalWitness for canonical structural verification. Retain compatibility with historical permutations of the witness source array. Do not trust an externally supplied event id without reconstruction. Unrecognized valid claims, including semantic-record.relation, contribute no record. For each recognized modern charge claim, require a four-field payload normalizable as SEAVT, existing eventForRow address/time correspondence, nonempty scalar seat, and causes from its verified core. Check content identity under the selected objectKind and decoded value, and decoded category equality. A valid row belonging to another kind/category is unselected; an invalid recognized row refuses the complete result.

For the legacy-import claim, require the exact L-O12 observation fields, claim/address/payload/reference correspondence, valid migration operator/time/causes, and exact artifact through the resolver. Reconstruct through F-R04 and compare supplied witness to that reconstruction after parseJournalWitness canonicalizes historical source-array order. Select by the original row's decoded category and content identity under the requested kind. Return the exact modern/imported union defined by L-O13, including outer null legacy attribution fields and nested custody metadata. Never use new migration metadata as old origin, time, causes or told.

Deduplicate only repeated witnesses with the same verified identity. If the same id is supplied with conflicting normalized observation/core/source content, refuse rather than arbitrarily select a representation. Separate verified events with equal content/time remain separate results. Use L-O13's explicit timestamp/non-timestamp and ordinal identity ordering. Do not expose the resolver or mutable source objects in results. The caller's bounded ports decide what parts may be disclosed; this internal projection is not a public route.

## F-R06 — Fabrication and independent receiving

Use the admitted source-patchset contract with one absent writable path `src/semiotic-eavt/semantic-record.mjs`, clause IDs F-R01–F-R06 and no deletions/edits. The exact Code root, missing target, all provided dependency bytes, this order, governing LLD, schema and fabrication/patchset contracts must be pinned before generation. The public packet includes read-only API/source evidence sufficient to reuse these primitives. Its private assessment and original host checkout are absent from the fresh isolated Luna generator.

Commit private receiving before invocation. Compute expected content/witness/artifact identities using existing primitives and original modern construction law, not the new functions as their oracle. Cover all four told states, relation distinction, ordinary witness identity and historical source permutations, equal content/time with opposing claims, construction versus admission, exact historical raw/custody occurrence, original versus migration time, missing attribution, resolver disappearance/failure, missing/malformed/altered records, input mutation and aggregate bounds. Demonstrate forbidden host imports/effects absent from the new module; no replacement host is accepted by these pure observations.

Assess the exact generated staged source under a network-denied namespace with explicitly bound read-only dependencies. Reject any behavioral failure without hand repair or private-assay feedback. Promotion requires revalidation of all current input bytes and continued target absence. Preserve candidate/provider/staging/receiving evidence. Integration must still migrate actual consumers, remove the old writer/read-through routes and prove storage/authority/application effects; promotion of this pure dependency does not satisfy those outstanding obligations.

title: Protected journal operation and source-view interfaces
date-created: 2026-09-27
type: specification
status: derived interface LLD; integrated fabrication and migration acceptance pending
derived-from: 2026-09-27-muse-assist-journal-storage-lld.md
derived-from-sha256: 0df0d58fd0c5ee2429547342311495b16c77d886672caaa5033a6ee7fab944b9
---

## Effect and ownership

Close L-S10's host-operation/source-view/barrier interface without changing the retained carrier, canonical identity or causal laws. A complete read, an ordinary append and a unique command admission must observe the same verified sources under one protected root operation. Personal context admission depends on that property when it checks current authority and retains an intent. Preserve the public `openJournal(settlementRoot)` path law and its ordinary read/fold/append capabilities. Remove independent segment/index authorities and Code-owned filesystem effects as L-S09 requires; a new owner behind an old read-through writer is unfinished.

The physical owner belongs in Systems `src/journal/filesystem/source-owner.mjs`. Existing public facade/operation modules call it. Code retains pure witness/command parsing and causal evaluation. Domain hosts receive bounded journal capabilities rather than the owner object or filesystem root. There is one owner mechanism for ordinary, unique, migration and recovery work; do not create a separate unique-command store or context database.

## L-O01 — Constructor and synchronous operation scope

The internal constructor is `openSourceOwner(storeDirectory)`, where storeDirectory is the explicit absolute physical journal directory obtained through L-H02's existing path laws. It validates/binds the root and host configuration but never initializes an absent store. Public `openJournal(root)` continues to take a settlement root; no second journal-directory suffix is added. Separate standalone stores retain their own admitted host configuration. Multiple owner objects referring to the same physical store use the same kernel gate and cannot execute concurrently, even within one process.

The owner exposes only `withOperation(perform)` to trusted System composition. It acquires the L-S04 gate, verifies root/lock/host identities, discovers and refreshes the complete bounded source view, invokes `perform(scope)` synchronously, checks identities again, constructs the result and releases its descriptor in a finally path. No user or model supplies perform. Detect a Promise/thenable return and refuse; never allow asynchronous host mutation to outlive the gate. A callback exception does not imply rollback of an already published source. Publication-uncertain precedence applies once publication may have occurred. No exception path unlinks the lock.

A scope is privately branded, belongs to that owner and operation epoch, and expires before lock release. Every method checks that lifetime. Retained scope objects, callbacks attempting a public nested operation, cross-owner use and reconstructed JSON objects cannot acquire authority; reentrant public access returns maintenance-busy. Pure immutable results may survive the scope; source handles, descriptors and durability evidence do not become reusable grants. Domain validation inside an operation receives this same scope and must not call a facade that reacquires the gate.

## L-O02 — Source view and exact selection

The scope provides `witness(eventRef)`, `artifact(artifactRef)`, `feeds(selection)`, `events(selection)`, `sourceStatus(feed)` and `sourceUsage()`. Arguments are closed immutable values checked against the shared reference/feed laws. `witness` returns a verified event's immutable normalized value and its derived admission state, or an explicit missing result; it does not erase original observation/source values retained for migration. `artifact` returns only an exactly verified canonical body or an explicit missing result. Corrupt recognized sources and IO failures throw the admitted JournalUnavailable diagnostic rather than appearing absent. These internal results do not authorize public disclosure.

A selection is exactly one of `{kind: "feed", feed}`, `{kind: "date", date}`, `{kind: "territory"}`, or `{kind: "as-of", feed, frontier}`. Date and frontier obey the existing journal address/causal laws, not a new time or reference interpretation. Feed/date/territory select their complete ordinary plus unique virtual membership, deduplicating by event identity within the selected union. Feed membership remains distinct where an event belongs to several feeds. As-of selects the verified causal closure of the exact frontier, intersected with the requested feed; a missing/blocked required frontier is evidence-unavailable, never an empty successful snapshot. An empty explicitly admitted frontier denotes the empty causal section only where the existing domain contract permits it.

`events` verifies the selected source set is complete under L-M10 before returning an array or invoking any public fold. Return causal topological order with ordinal event-identity ties for unrelated events, using the existing causal graph laws. A pending/blocked witness in a complete feed/date/territory selection prevents a successful complete result, without requiring unrelated feeds to be ready for a feed read. Exact-reference/as-of reads require their exact closure. Root-level source corruption still prevents claiming a complete scan. Fold callbacks see no rows before completeness is established; caller folds are synchronous and cannot reenter the owner.

`feeds({kind: "date", date})` and `feeds({kind: "territory"})` return verified membership locators, including feeds supplied solely by unique-slot sources. Discovery does not assert their causal completeness. `sourceStatus(feed)` is exactly L-M01's closed result and uses the same protected view as any combined statement-information observation. `sourceUsage()` returns the internal closed `{sourceFiles, sourceBytes}` root-custody measurement from L-M03, with nonnegative safe integers and each physical source counted once. It is absent from public feed/context ports. No filesystem pathname is an event locator or proof of authority.

## L-O03 — Publication and readiness

The scope's `publishRetained(entries)` accepts only verified L-S01 entries from trusted journal construction or maintenance. Arbitrary remote requests cannot submit obstruction entries. Canonicalize with the existing codec, sort/deduplicate exact entries, enforce configured bounds, compute the exact complete-batch digest and use the accepted create-only durable helper. A nonempty valid batch is the publication unit; do not silently split an oversized batch or drop a witness to fit a budget. A domain may explicitly construct several bounded batches where its own atomicity/acknowledgment contract allows that.

Return internal `{disposition, digest, retainedEvents, admittedEvents}` with disposition `created` or `existing`, and ordinal unique event-reference arrays. `retainedEvents` means event identities newly given source custody by this operation; `admittedEvents` means identities newly entering the admitted state after refresh, including formerly pending events unlocked by the new source. Neither is inferred merely from batch creation. Adding a second feed membership to an already known event changes membership without pretending the event itself is newly retained/admitted. Adapters preserve their existing result's feed-specific meaning using the before/after view; do not equate these root-wide deltas with every facade's `written` count.

After publication refresh the same protected view to its bounded fixed point. No persistent admitted/pending/dependent index is written as authority. A pending source is durably retained but is not a successful causal admission. New source discovery must be visible to the next operation without restart/cache deletion; removed/changed immutable sources cannot be hidden by a warm cache. Cache only verified immutable values keyed by exact digest and physical identity, and reverify required closure bytes for acknowledgment.

## L-O04 — Closure durability

The scope's `requireDurable({events, artifacts, uniqueSlot})` accepts ordinal distinct verified reference sets; uniqueSlot is either null or the exact parsed unique-slot address under this journal. It expands the full required causal/artifact closure, verifies semantic state and exact source bytes, and synchronizes every required source and directory through the admitted ancestor barrier. Shared files are synchronized once; every required semantic reference remains represented. Exceeding any configured count/byte/depth budget is resource-limit; unresolved or blocked required material is evidence-unavailable. A digest-cache hit cannot stand in for a durability barrier.

The success value is opaque internal barrier evidence privately bound to this scope epoch and the complete sorted event/artifact/source-digest sets plus journal identity. No boolean `durable` argument or serialized prior receipt can replace it. It cannot be reused after gate release or for a different closure. Source publication for pending evidence uses the create-only helper's source-custody durability, not a forged successful admitted-closure result. Maintenance receipt/inventory sources likewise require their actual bytes durable before deletion; they are not required to invent admitted witness relationships for every historical pending item.

A facade returns a durable admission acknowledgment only after its requested admitted closure barrier succeeds. If source publication might be visible but the refresh/barrier/final binding check fails, return publication-uncertain as required by L-J06. Preserve visible bytes and permit later verified recovery; never remove them to imply rollback. For an already occupied unique slot, barrier the original retained command and its closure, not the conflicting proposed command.

## L-O05 — Registered unique domains and authority under protection

Unique admission is a trusted domain capability layered on this owner, not a general public `appendUnique` route. At host construction, bind an immutable domain registration naming `interaction` or `effect-successor`, its exact pure command validator, authenticated-principal source and protected-view new/occupied authority checks. The registration is an in-process capability kept by the Systems/domain composition; requests cannot select a validator, replace callbacks or supply an approved verdict. Do not infer production admission from a fixture registration.

The domain entry first validates canonical command identity and its trusted caller/context association, then enters this owner's operation. Resolve current authority against the supplied protected view; no asynchronous inference or network authorization is performed while holding the gate. The occupied path separately authorizes resolution before returning any reference, verifies the original record with `parseUniqueJournalRecord`, completes its closure barrier and returns existing/conflict by exact canonical-command correspondence. A denied resolver receives no occupied identity. A missing slot is an internal observation used only by the admitted creation path.

For a vacant slot, the registered new-transition check proves the exact predecessor/assignment/proposal/authority conditions required by its domain. Construct through `addressUniqueJournalCommand` and `uniqueJournalRecord`, barrier the necessary predecessor/artifacts, publish create-only, refresh, barrier the full retained closure and return created only to the live successful publisher. Unexpected occupancy despite exclusion takes the verified occupied path and never returns created. Keep public storage outcomes exactly L-J06's four variants and seven reasons. Domain refusal remains the domain's invalid/forbidden result before any source mutation; it is not a new storage-unavailable reason. The adapter must preserve this distinction rather than flattening every exception into an absent slot.

The concrete interaction and effect validators remain derived from their respective LLDs. Registration shape does not establish their correctness. Production unique dispatch stays unmounted until their source contracts and independent observations are accepted; a fixture may exercise storage with clearly labeled fixture authority.

## L-O06 — Facade migration and capability preservation

Adapt `FilesystemJournal` and root-independent `journal` methods to enter the owner once per complete operation. Internal helpers use the already-held scope. Preserve `read`, `readAsOf`, row/causal/date/territory folds, verified artifact resolution, feed discovery and ordinary append effects, with the explicit L-M measurement/diagnostic refinements. `journal.feed` remains a pure address constructor; obtaining a handle grants no read/write permission. Do not make `openJournal` provision a store or return an apparently empty source after a host error.

Packet/head/derived projection functions are not new source authorities. Follow each actual consumer: data necessary for work/recovery must be retained as verified source information; reproducible projections may be regenerated or removed. Do not preserve a mutable head because of its filename, nor silently delete a meaningful record under the label cache. Replace `compact` and old segment/index/read-through machinery with the single bounded L-S09 maintenance migration. The final runtime refuses legacy custody rather than silently migrating it on a read.

Migration inventory must include semantic-record legacy `data/logs` carriers and every `.js` as well as `.mjs` consumer. The recovered corpus-management command programs write activity/provenance/territory records; the legacy linguistic adapter records readdressing evidence. Preserve those effects. Their filesystem/process composition belongs in Systems; merely changing their Data-layer imports upward to Systems violates the dependency order. Keep pure contracts/value transformations in their proper lower layer, migrate actual command/skill/package callers with the host capability, and preserve their recorded evidence before retiring old writers. The consumer evidence bound below identifies these additional paths; it is not authorization to rename directories without following their execution entrypoints.

## L-O07 — Receiving obligations

The integrated source order binds this interface with L-S01–L-S10, L-H01–L-H07, L-M01–L-M10 and L-J01–L-J09. The integrated order must bind every applicable predecessor obligation. Observe actual owner exclusion/release across processes and owner death; scope expiry/reentrancy; malformed/changed source refusal; cold/warm agreement; pending-to-admitted recovery; unique-only feeds; complete read refusal before callbacks; unchanged ordinary causal results; source-versus-closure durability failures; same/conflicting unique retries; and byte-custody comparison before every legacy deletion. Inspect required retained files and independent reconstructed outcomes.

No successful unit observation constitutes production domain authority, migration acceptance or a working assistant. Still close the complete consumer/entrypoint changes, storage fabrication packet and private assay commitment; then generate and independently assess the connected realization. The source module/interface specified here is not a handwritten implementation or a new compatibility layer.

## L-O08 — Semantic-record effects and layer split

The useful semantic-record effect is to retain/recover a content-identified JSON value under an object kind/category, with observation time, independent support/opposition, optional relation, origin and causal references. Its physical journal location and helper wrappers are not separate capabilities. Preserve content identity through the existing `identifyJsonSemanticContent`/EMPTY_WITNESS_ROOT and SEN row/claim laws. Relation rows remain distinct from record rows. A predicate-shaped relation cannot be mistaken for another record.

Generate the pure constructor/projection in Code `src/semiotic-eavt/semantic-record.mjs`, deriving from the current record/query/admit implementations while removing filesystem, process and path effects. Its construction input is the semantic fields only: objectKind, category, record, recordedAt, told, optional relation, causes and origin. It produces the existing content identity and structurally verified, unpersisted witness candidates, with no root, time acquisition or publication. Such construction does not prove causal admission, storage or durability. Preserve recordedAt as the row’s original JSON t; for modern witness identity only, preserve the existing eventForRow boundary-time mapping String(t). That conversion cannot replace the original time in the row or query result. The host supplies an explicit authenticated origin for authority-sensitive new records; the historical omitted-origin objectKind convention conveys no authenticated principal authority. Its projection consumes explicit verified witnesses and an exact objectKind/category selection; it performs no dated-directory scan. Pure schema checks/template binding stay below Systems and do not acquire storage merely because a template contains a root field.

The Systems owner at `src/journal/semantic-record.mjs` binds those transformations to the admitted journal facade and exposes the necessary record/query/settlement convenience capability. Host command entrypoints own stdin, environment, root selection and output; none remain in the Code module. Existing application/System/organizational consumers migrate to the System capability. Code and Networking consumers must either receive the bounded record/query ports from their host or move their host composition into Systems. No re-export shim from Code to Systems survives.

Migrate the actual old host family, not only two imports: `record-semantic-record`, `query-semantic-records`, `admit-semantic-record`, `record-configured-semantic-record`, `check-semantic-record-references`, `check-semantic-record-responses`, and the `command.mjs` dispatch entries that select them. The checks combine file traversal/time with record queries today; isolate their pure predicates and put the complete IO operation in the System command composition. Bind package exports/bin mappings, configured command references and documentation/skill entrypoints before deleting their old host implementations. Do not change semantic-identity primitives or unrelated pure SEN commands as collateral cleanup.

## L-O09 — Preserve observation distinctions and legacy uncertainty

The current query merges legacy and witnessed records and deduplicates by `[record.id, recordedAt]`, returning the first. Retire that rule: two witnesses with equal record content/time can have different support/opposition, origins, claims and causes. Keep distinct verified event identities. Deduplicate only repeated custody of the same verified event; preserve its several feed memberships in the source view. Sort record projections by the explicit L-O13 recorded-time ordering, then ordinal observation identity, never locale-sensitive file-order precedence. Callers wanting distinct content values must explicitly project that view after evidence-sensitive decisions; storage cannot erase contrary observations for them.

Legacy `data/logs/**/witness-journal-seavt.jsonl` rows contain record/time material without modern told/origin/causal attribution. Their absence is not an implicit held assertion. Migration must retain their values, original times and complete row distinctions, together with exact source-file digest and row occurrence in the custody inventory. Equal row values in different source occurrences remain attributable custody observations until a domain-specific equivalence is proven. Modern witnesses cannot be suppressed by the existence of an older row with the same content/time.

L-O11–L-O13 define the concrete import representation and pure projection required before these legacy files can be removed. They distinguish an imported historical row from an originally attributed witness. Any new migration witness attributes the act of migration to its admitted operator and time; it cannot fabricate the original author's identity, support/opposition or causes. A legacy-only query must retain its usable content/time while exposing unavailable attribution, rather than disguising new migration metadata as original evidence. These contracts do not permit runtime legacy read-through. The custody receipt includes the verified legacy source and replacement correspondence under L-S09. Uninterpretable rows block retirement, and mere inability to discover a live writer is not proof it is quiescent.

The three recovered corpus-management programs currently send `charge: {support, refutation}` to an implementation requiring `told: {for, against}`. A direct non-mutating invocation of the current writer confirms it rejects that request before root resolution/publication. Migrate each actual caller explicitly: support maps to for and refutation maps to against, preserving both independent booleans. Missing fields refuse; never add a positive default merely to make old callers appear to work. Claims about prior successful records require inspection of actual stored evidence, not the presence of these programs.

## L-O10 — Connected host entrypoints and retirement evidence

`corpus-management-service` has observed package bins and script/skill wrappers for manage-project-corpus-knowledge and prior-research solicitation/invocation. Preserve their ActivityStreams response, bounded source recovery, provenance and journaled outcome effects in Systems-owned host operations. Update the existing wrappers, package mappings and skill entrypoints to the new host command. Data retains schemas and declared facts; executable pure transformations belong in Code, rather than treating their current Data directory as permanent ownership. Do not introduce a reverse Data-to-Systems import to preserve an old wrapper.

The sweep program has a direct process/argument interface even though no package/skill/non-test caller was found. Absence of an indexed caller does not prove its useful directory classification, territory derivation, coordination and evidence-recording effects are obsolete. Account for that direct invocation in the migration and decide its surviving host exposure from those effects; do not invent an additional service or silently delete it. The legacy linguistic readdressing adapter already belongs to Systems; keep its pure legacy admission distinct from its filesystem read and receipt-recording operation, adapting the latter to the shared journal. Its lack of discovered non-test importers is a retrieval result, not proof of operational disuse.

Networking sale-ledger derivation accepts bounded journal ports from the actual HTTP/CLI host. X402 seller/facilitator/market command and process composition belongs in Systems; update package commands, deployment/container and service-unit entrypoints alongside it. The Code-layer npm publication command likewise composes host IO and journal evidence in Systems while preserving the publication decision/recording effect. Confirm these concrete callers before source deletion; moving filenames without their runtime entrypoints is not retirement.

The bound consumer search includes `.js`, `.mjs` and package JSON references, plus separately traced skill/script callers. Its classifications aid fabrication and are not a replacement operational registry or proof that dynamic imports/human command invocations do not exist. Revalidate the actual selected entrypoints and source hashes in the integrated order. Receiving evidence must show useful records can be written/read with original distinctions, the same commands still deliver their outcomes, lower layers have no upward host imports, and old segment/legacy writers are absent from the surviving execution paths. The L-O11–L-O13 import contracts and complete adapter/assay closure must be bound into the integrated storage packet before calling it generation-ready.

## L-O11 — Exact historical row custody

Refining L-S09 and L-O09, import each interpretable nonblank physical line as one ordinary content-addressed artifact, using the existing addressArtifact/verifyArtifact and retained-artifact carrier. Its closed value is `{kind:"metroplat.journal.legacy-seavt-row",version:1,source:{path,sha256,bytes},line,offset,length,raw,row}`. The accompanying `2026-09-27-muse-assist-legacy-row.schema.json` closes the representation; the correspondence rules here are additional semantic obligations, not established by schema validation alone. No new retained-source family, mutable lookup or side database is introduced.

source identifies the complete stable legacy file: path is settlement-root-relative with slash separators, no empty, dot, dot-dot or absolute components, no NUL or backslash; sha256 is the lowercase SHA-256 of all original bytes, including separators; bytes is their safe-integer length. These are custody metadata, not permission to read an arbitrary pathname. The host opens only the maintenance inventory's verified regular file under its admitted root, checks identity and exact bytes before and after extraction, and holds old writers quiescent. Missing/unreadable/changed inputs refuse; the old reader's empty-result and skip-malformed behavior is not permitted.

Split the exact bytes at LF. line is the one-based physical line number, including blank lines; offset is the zero-based byte offset of that line's first byte; length is the number of bytes before LF, or to EOF for the last unterminated line. raw is that exact line decoded as strict UTF-8, with no BOM stripping, replacement decoding, trimming, Unicode normalization or CR removal. UTF-8 encoding raw must reproduce the slice exactly; offset+length cannot exceed source.bytes. A CR in CRLF is part of raw. A terminal LF does not invent another record. Blank lines contain only JSON whitespace (space, tab, CR, or empty); account for them in the comparison inventory but create no semantic record for them. All remaining lines must parse as bounded JSON with duplicate keys rejected and normalize through the existing EAVT and closed/typed SEN admission laws. row is the exact normalized `{e,a,v,t}` value; no timestamp coercion or value repair occurs. The original tuple/object form and lexical representation remain in raw.

Keep equal rows at different line offsets or source paths as separate custody observations. The artifact's whole-value identity includes that occurrence. Preserve time as the original JSON value, including non-string times admitted by the old row contract. Do not select an object kind from a filename: kind is established only by the existing content-identity law when projecting for an explicit query kind. Retain valid non-record/relation rows too, even when a semantic-record query does not select them. They require their own consumer correspondence before retirement.

The existing JSON resource envelope and host line/batch/closure limits apply to raw, normalized row and their combined canonical artifact/witness size. Preflight the whole input before removing anything. An oversized, duplicate-key, invalid UTF-8, malformed JSON or inadmissible SEN row blocks retirement of the source and reports its occurrence; it cannot be skipped, truncated, silently repaired or assigned a new meaning. This is bounded refusal, not a claim that every historical file has been migrated. Bind actual corpus sizes and all refusal cases in the fabrication order. Original bytes remain in place whenever necessary interpretation or capacity is unresolved.

## L-O12 — Migration observation, separate from original evidence

The trusted maintenance host constructs a journalWitness for each imported-row artifact. Its observation is exactly `{kind:"metroplat.journal.observation",seat:operator,claim:tm.mark("semantic-record.legacy-import"),address:tm.mark(rowArtifact.ref),time:importedAt,causes:migrationCauses,payload:{kind:"metroplat.journal.legacy-import",version:1,row:rowArtifact.ref},referencedArtifacts:[rowArtifact.ref]}`. operator is the authenticated maintenance principal; importedAt is the actual migration observation's exact UTC millisecond timestamp. migrationCauses is the explicitly bound ordinal distinct verified causal-reference set, possibly empty where maintenance has no causal predecessor. Neither historical row time nor guessed author supplies these fields. Do not use semantic-record.held/unknown/denied/contested: the claim is custody import, not an assertion of the old content.

The immutable maintenance input binds operator, importedAt, migrationCauses and destination feed before publication. Resume the same input by verifying actual bytes and existing witnesses; do not regenerate time on each retry. The configured destination is a verified journal feed under existing path laws, recorded in the custody comparison. It is a custody feed, not an invented historical object-kind/date feed. Semantic projection selects imported rows from the same owner view across this membership; it must not require them to appear in a modern kind's old physical segment path. An authorized later distinct custody observation may coexist and remains distinguishable.

Retain both the row artifact and migration witness through L-S01. The witness's external artifact reference must resolve to the exact verified artifact; a missing/mismatching body is evidence-unavailable/source-corrupt as appropriate, never an empty legacy result. Verify the full closure and barrier it before acknowledging the import. Constructing a valid witness does not prove that an arbitrary remote party observed the legacy file: only the admitted maintenance host can exercise this import capability. Public generic append cannot manufacture accepted legacy custody merely by choosing the claim text.

Extend the L-S09 canonical comparison inventory with the source's physical line census and, for every interpreted nonblank occurrence, `{line,offset,length,rowArtifact,event,feed}`. Account explicitly for blank line spans and final delimiter state. Before deletion, independently reread each original slice, reconstruct/verify its row artifact and migration witness, compare the original row and usable query projection, and prove that no nonblank occurrence was omitted. Persist this inventory through the existing receipt's capabilities reference; retain source digest/length and replacement batch correspondence under L-S09. A successful publication alone is insufficient deletion evidence.

## L-O13 — Query projection and acceptance distinctions

Systems supplies the selection from its active L-O01 branded scope, after proving the selected witnesses admitted. The pure Code function cannot authenticate that provenance or confer admission by inspecting a caller-provided flag. The pure semantic-record projection in L-O08 consumes those witnesses plus an explicit artifact resolver over the already verified owner view; the resolver performs no filesystem IO and cannot consult a second root. For an imported witness, require the exact L-O12 structure, row-artifact reference correspondence and L-O11 artifact laws. Decode the category/value/entity using the existing SEN codec, require the selected category, and verify the entity equals identifyJsonSemanticContent for the explicitly selected objectKind and EMPTY_WITNESS_ROOT. A legitimate nonmatching row is unselected; malformed claimed import evidence fails the complete query rather than disappearing.

A selected imported result is exactly `{id,objectKind,category,recordedAt,record,told:null,event:null,origin:null,causes:null,attribution:{kind:"unavailable",reason:"legacy-row"},custody:{kind:"legacy-import",event,operator,importedAt,causes,rowArtifact,source,line,offset,length}}`. The outer time/value/id come from the old row. The nested event/operator/time/causes describe only migration. null means original attribution was not available; it is neither `{for:false,against:false}` nor an empty original causal set. No caller may authorize work or count a supporting/contrary assertion from that absence. An independent later appraisal can add an attributed witness without rewriting history.

Modern record results preserve `{id,objectKind,category,recordedAt,record,told,event,origin,causes}` and add `attribution:{kind:"witnessed"}` and `custody:null`. These two variants form an explicit query result union. Consumers inspecting truth/authority must branch on attribution; content-only recovery may explicitly extract record/time from either. Projection is an internal capability: source.path and host custody metadata are not automatically exposed through personal-context or public query routes.

Retain distinct modern witness identities and distinct imported custody witness identities. Repeated membership of one verified witness produces one result, while distinct imports of one occurrence remain distinct custody observations. Order exact UTC millisecond timestamps chronologically using their validated representation; those precede other historical JSON times. Order other times by ordinal canonical JSON text, explicitly without asserting chronology; then order ties by the modern event or custody event reference. Never use localeCompare, String coercion, input file order or migration time to replace the original time. Preserve callers' need for causal processing through the journal's causal view rather than claiming this display ordering is causal order.

Independent receiving must exercise tuple and object rows, CRLF and unterminated final lines, blank-line accounting, duplicate equal rows at separate occurrences, the same content/time with opposing modern witnesses, legacy-only content recovery, non-string historical time, relation/nonmatching rows, interrupted/resumed import, changed/missing file and artifact bodies, malformed/duplicate-key/invalid-UTF-8/oversized refusal, and removal only after exact occurrence correspondence. The current-reader fixture bound in evidence demonstrates silent malformed-line loss and missing-file empty success; it is migration evidence, not acceptance of a replacement. Representation validation likewise is not runtime acceptance. The connected source order, generated implementation and independent receiving remain required.

## What this is

This LLD closes H-F2/H-F3's first source-derivation realization using existing inference and isolation tools, without adding a scheduler, gateway, generator framework, or application-specific fabricator. It governs an operator-mediated transformation from a closed fabrication order into a staged candidate and separately held acceptance evidence. It is a bounded first realization, not automation of the whole Customer Demand-to-code chain.

## Work-order and candidate carriers

**L-F01.** The admitted generation input MUST bind the predecessor chain, fabrication order, current transformation-input bytes/digests, public examples, output contract, model/configuration and invocation bounds. The input MUST exclude private assay source, fixtures, expected results and assessor conversation. A separate assessor MUST derive and commit the private assay inventory before source derivation starts. Commitment is a byte digest, not proof that the assay is sufficient.

**L-F02.** The first output contract is a closed JSON object with `disposition` (`candidate` or `refused`), `reason`, and `edits`. A refused result MUST have no edits and a specific reason. Each candidate edit MUST contain exactly `path`, `inputSha256`, `before`, `after`, and `clauses`. `path` identifies an admitted relative source file, `inputSha256` binds its original bytes, `before` is a nonempty exact substring occurring once at the point of application, `after` is replacement text, and `clauses` is a nonempty array of governing clause IDs. Multiple edits to a file apply in output order against one original input digest. Missing files, ambiguous text matches, path escape, mismatched input digest, unrecognized clause IDs, or extra object fields MUST refuse materialization. Candidate outputs are untrusted source until independently assessed.

The deterministic materializer applies only admitted textual replacements to a staged copy and computes full resulting file digests. This is a bounded codemod application, not behavioral source derivation. It MUST NOT execute generator-provided shell commands. New files require a separately specified creation contract; this first work order uses existing files. Actual transformed bytes, input/output digests and clause correspondence become the source-result evidence required by H-F2/F-H07.

## Generator access boundary

**L-F03.** The source provider MUST run in a fresh inference context with no inherited conversation, no assessor material, and no shared-checkout write access. For the first local realization, the existing Codex executable MAY be invoked noninteractively with the requested GPT-6 Luna model inside a Bubblewrap mount/PID namespace. The only task content is the public input packet delivered on standard input. The host checkout, assay directory, host process namespace, session history, user/project configuration, skills and connectors MUST NOT be mounted or otherwise supplied. The public output schema MAY be mounted read-only. Runtime libraries, TLS/DNS files and the existing authentication file may be made available solely to run the authenticated provider; authentication material MUST NOT be printed or placed in prompts.

The invocation MUST use a fresh ephemeral session, ignore user configuration and rules, disable shell, web search, apps and further agent delegation where the installed CLI supports those controls, and use a read-only model-command sandbox. External process isolation supplies the filesystem boundary; prompts and the CLI's read-only setting alone do not. Native tools which remain advertised cannot see the omitted mounts. The invocation MUST NOT resume this conversation or any previous source/assessor session. The actual argument vector, executable digest/version, public input digest, observed model and event record MUST be retained without credentials. Undeclared tool use, unexpected mounts, source input change, unavailable authentication/model, or source-provider access to assessor material MUST reject that invocation. No alternate model is silently substituted.

**L-F04.** Before live source generation, a deterministic process under the same mount profile MUST establish that the host checkout and an external sentinel cannot be read, that the process view is namespaced, and that only the intended task inputs are available. This demonstrates the local process boundary, not provider-server confidentiality or model correctness. The provider's own server retention/isolation remains a trust assumption and MUST be stated. The operator MUST NOT send private assay content through feedback, diagnostics or a resumed source session.

## Independent assessment and promotion

**L-F05.** The assessor MUST run the committed assays against the content-bound candidate, separately from the source provider. Executing candidate code MUST not give it a communication channel back to that provider or access to operational credentials/private user data. A network-denied execution namespace with only required runtime, dependency, candidate and assay inputs is the selected local assessment boundary. The assessor may inspect private results; the source generator receives only a separately admitted public reproduction or changed specification, never private fixtures or raw assay logs.

**L-F06.** The evidence bundle MUST contain specification/chain/input/candidate/assay digests, provider/model/configuration, invocation boundaries, method, environment, assessor, result, limits, and measured token/time/cost information where available. Missing cash-cost data MUST be marked unavailable rather than zero. Generic artifact receipts may reference this bundle by locator/digest; receipts do not prove acceptance. Failed candidates remain rejected. New evidence or revised specifications can justify a new candidate; an invisible edit after a failed assay cannot.

**L-F07.** Promotion MUST compare each original input digest with current shared-checkout bytes immediately before applying the accepted replacements. Any mismatch refuses the entire promotion batch and preserves both candidate and concurrent edits. All affected files must pass this check before any is replaced. Promotion MUST retain the accepted output digest and actual receiving-workflow evidence; staging checks do not establish public deployment or assistant operation.

## Implementations

The installed host currently has Bubblewrap and Codex CLI 0.154.0. A preliminary empty namespace probe could not see `/home/emsenn/info`; the complete invocation profile still requires L-F04's recorded check. The CLI's local help exposes ephemeral, ignored-user-config, output-schema and noninteractive execution. [Official configuration documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference) defines the shell-tool switch; [noninteractive documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/non-interactive-mode) describes the ephemeral invocation. These are invocation capabilities, not proof of assay independence or generated-code correctness.

The separately inspected ops inference route reported one configured `llama3.2:3b` provider with no admitted resource-availability observation. It was not invoked or substituted for the requested Luna source role. Its existence is not evidence of available capacity. The local invocation above uses existing tooling; no inference service is being repaired or reimplemented here.

## Open questions

- **L-FO1:** The first source invocation must establish actual model/authentication availability and record L-F04's complete boundary check. Failure preserves the closed order and assays; it does not authorize direct hand coding.
- **L-FO2:** Broader unattended generation, scheduler integration and automatic demand-to-design derivation are not supplied by this operator-mediated protocol. Any subsequent automation must preserve these contracts and receive its own specification before implementation.

## Necessary transformation

L-F02's exact-substring contract cannot create a System module or retire its superseded Code implementation. L-S06/L-S09 require both effects, including consumer migration. This order extends the deterministic materialization boundary for explicitly declared source creation and deletion. It does not add a scheduler, model harness, repository mutation service or product-code generator. Existing edit-only orders and their evidence remain unchanged. The source provider continues deriving behavioral source; the operator's deterministic materializer performs only declared byte transformations on a fresh staged directory.

**F-P01 — Opt-in input.** A patchset work order binds an exact source root and an input inventory. The inventory is a JSON object with exactly `kind`, `version`, `sourceRoot`, `files`, `clauses`. Kind is `source-patchset-input`; version is integer 1. SourceRoot is an absolute existing directory. Files is a path-keyed object. Every key is an admitted relative POSIX source path: nonempty components, each matching `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+`, no dot/dot-dot component, absolute prefix, backslash or NUL. Each descriptor is exactly either `{state:"present",sha256}` or `{state:"absent"}`. Present entries bind lowercase SHA-256 of original bytes; absent entries authorize only creation. No path may be an ancestor of another admitted path. Clauses is a nonempty unique list of recognized nonempty clause-ID strings. Existing paths must be ordinary regular files and all existing ancestors, including the root's own path, must be nonsymlink directories; absent paths must also have no symlink or nondirectory ancestor. The inventory is trusted work-order input, not generated permission to touch files.

The concrete storage order must enumerate its exact writable files and clause IDs before source generation. This generic extension grants no writable source path by itself. Read-only dependencies and governing specification hashes remain protected under L-F01/L-F07 and are additional to this writable inventory.

**F-P02 — Closed candidate.** The new opt-in output is exactly `{kind:"source-patchset",version:1,disposition,reason,changes}`. Disposition is `candidate` or `refused`; reason is a string. A refusal has zero changes. A candidate has at least one change. Each admitted path occurs at most once, and every change contains a nonempty unique `clauses` array drawn from the inventory. No generated shell command, URL, dependency installation, permission change or recursive delete operation exists.

Changes are exactly one of:

- `{operation:"edit",path,inputSha256,replacements,clauses}` against a present entry. Each replacement is exactly `{before,after}`. Before is nonempty text occurring exactly once when that replacement is applied; after is text. Apply replacements in order against the original bound UTF-8 text. The one input digest remains the original file digest, not an intermediate value. The list is nonempty.
- `{operation:"create",path,text,clauses}` against an absent entry. Text is complete strict UTF-8 source, supplied by the generator; the operator must not fill behavioral placeholders. Creation emits an ordinary file with mode 0644. An executable entrypoint should normally be invoked through its existing runtime; changing execution bits requires a separately admitted order.
- `{operation:"delete",path,inputSha256,clauses}` against a present entry. This removes that exact file from the staged result. It does not delete directories, follow links, delete imports automatically or authorize removing unlisted data. Necessary consumer and export changes must appear as separately bound changes in the same work family.

All objects are closed. Reject Boolean values masquerading as integer versions, unknown operations, malformed digests, repeated paths, unknown clauses, invalid UTF-8, missing inputs, changed input bytes or an unexpectedly present creation target. Do not normalize generated paths or repair a refused candidate.

**F-P03 — Validate before staging.** The materializer rechecks every inventory entry, including unchanged inputs, before creating any staged output. It validates the whole candidate and calculates all intended output bytes in memory before writing. A malformed candidate therefore leaves no stage directory. It may inspect file metadata and bytes, but it never imports, evaluates or executes candidate text. The only mechanical transformations are the specified text replacements, creation and file omission.

Use a fresh nonexistent stage directory outside the source root. A stage ancestor cannot be a symlink or non-directory. The operator chooses that path; it is not accepted from the candidate. Copy each unchanged admitted present file and each resulting changed file into the stage at its declared relative path, preserving the existing file's permission bits for retained/edited files. Deleted inputs are omitted and their digests/modes retained in the receipt. Do not copy the repository's unbounded contents or leave links from the stage into the working checkout. Recheck all original inputs after staging before writing the staged result receipt. A concurrent change invalidates the stage and prevents acceptance; it does not authorize changing the concurrent work.

A host I/O error during staging may leave a partial staged directory. It must have no successful receipt; report failure and preserve it for inspection. Do not represent staging as an atomic multi-file filesystem transaction. A retry uses a fresh stage and fresh validation rather than overwriting an uncertain directory.

**F-P04 — Staged receipt and assessment.** The operator writes a sibling `<stage>.receipt.json` only after successful validation/staging/revalidation. The receipt contains kind `source-patchset-stage`, integer version 1, inventory/candidate digests, the materializer digest, each original path's presence/digest/mode, each final path's presence/digest/mode, and disposition `staged-unaccepted`. No receipt claims product acceptance or promotion. A receipt target already present refuses before staging; receipt creation is exclusive. A receipt write failure is a failed stage operation even if all source files have been written.

Independent assessment uses the exact staged tree plus explicitly admitted read-only dependencies. A retired file must be absent from that assessment namespace; a fallback mount of the old checkout must not make deleted code available again. Verify source creation, changed consumers and actual retired routes, not only that new files load. The private assessment remains excluded from source generation under L-F03–L-F05. Source provider and materializer receive no permission to amend acceptance fixtures after a failure.

**F-P05 — Promotion remains separate.** This materializer has no shared-checkout mutation or deployment mode. Product promotion remains governed by L-F07 plus the concrete work order's creation/deletion preconditions. Recheck all present/absent expectations before touching any target. Do not delete an obsolete file unless the complete affected capability and consumer migration have independently passed. A staged tree, deleted-path list or model assertion is insufficient. A multi-file promotion must record partial host failure accurately; it must not claim atomicity that the filesystem mechanism does not provide. Never restore over unrelated concurrent edits while trying to roll back a partial operation.

**F-P06 — Independent mechanical observations.** Demonstrate in disposable files that one batch creates a new file, changes an exact unique substring, retires a bound old file and carries an unchanged input, while leaving the source root byte-identical. Exercise stale/absent mismatch, ambiguous replacement, malformed/extra fields, repeated changes, unknown clause, path traversal, symlink input/ancestor, a path ancestor collision, malformed UTF-8 and an existing stage/receipt. Invalid input must produce no successful receipt or shared source mutation. The observations verify deterministic materialization only; they do not accept any journal or assistant behavior.

The initial realization may be a small operator-owned script retained with the fabrication evidence and invoked directly. It is not a new runtime package. This is mechanical tooling under the closed contract above; all product behavioral text in real candidates must still originate from the admitted isolated source-generation process.

apiFacts.SEN: jsonToTerm(value) encodes JSON to a closed typed SEN term; termToJson(term) recovers JSON; tm.mark(string) constructs a closed typed mark. identifyJsonSemanticContent({objectKind,value,witnessRoot:EMPTY_WITNESS_ROOT}).id is the existing JSON semantic identity. All are named exports at the relative paths specified in the order.
apiFacts.json: admitCanonicalJson(raw, JSON_RESOURCE_ENVELOPE) returns {value,text,byteLength} and rejects duplicate JSON names. canonicalizeJson(value,envelope) returns a deeply frozen snapshot in value.
apiFacts.artifact: addressArtifact(value) and verifyArtifact(ref,text) return {ref,canonical:{value,text,byteLength}}; verifyArtifact accepts noncanonical equivalent text so compare its canonical.text to supplied text explicitly.
